title: Quantization throughput safeguard sweep and regression detector
creator: Anika Rao
description: Goal: Build a repeatable cross-workload quantization benchmarking harness that measures tokens/sec and p95 latency under real-ish traffic profiles and ties those perf signals to quality deltas (semantic similarity + task-level metrics) so we can automatically detect regressions when introducing FP16/INT8/INT4 variants. Deliverables: (1) end-to-end harness that runs scheduled sweeps across model families and quant profiles; (2) regression detector that raises alerts when perf or quality moves outside thresholds; (3) dashboards and runbook for interpreting failures and triage playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run 3 workload templates (chat, completion, embed) for a given model+quant profile and produce tokens/sec + p95 + quality metrics in a single run
Regression detector flags a run when tokens/sec drops >5% relative to baseline OR p95 > 1.5x baseline OR semantic-similarity drops >0.025 absolute
Outputs are persisted to perf-store and visible in runtime-1.22 perf dashboard with links to artifacts
Automated nightly sweep runs for top-10 customer models and creates a ticket when regression is detected
approach: We will implement a portable runner that composes: workload generator (client-side replayer with sequence-length distribution), system profiler (tokens/sec, CPU/GPU util, mem), latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), and eval harness for quality (embedding cosine similarity against gold, and task-specific checks for reasoning prompts). Runs will use the same seed prompt set used by Optimize/evals. Regression detector appliance computes relative deltas vs a stored baseline snapshot and uses a simple rule engine plus a lightweight statistical test (bootstrap on embedding similarities) to suppress noisy alerts. Start with FP16 and INT8 runs, include INT4 for smaller models with a guarded gating rule. For INT4, we also run soft-fallback runs that re-run a subset with INT8 for comparison.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Initial spike: validated that replayed workloads produce stable tokens/sec on cpu/GPU dev clusters; saw 12% variance for long completions when batch size changed
2026-02-27 - Decision: Use embedding cosine (SBERT-base) as primary semantic similarity measure for sweep; fallback to task-specific EM/F1 for evaluation suites where available
2026-03-02 - PR #1423 opened with harness runner and basic bootstrap-based regression test; reviewers: Priya, Omar. Running CI perf runs nightly in workflow.

2026-03-05 - Observed INT8 on model-rx2 shows 6% tokens/sec improvement but a 0.03 drop in semantic similarity on reasoning prompts. Marked as a candidate for targeted layer-wise quantization adjustments.
2026-03-09 - Rolled threshold update: semantic-similarity drop threshold tightened from 0.03 to 0.025 after discussing signal noise with Eval team
2026-03-12 - Work in progress: adding thermal-aware scheduling to reduce p95 spikes during sustained sweeps; next: wire alerts to #eng-quant and auto-create Linear tickets when detector fires
